From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-signature MAP: phased migration, canary & eval checkpoints (Aperture Health)

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday and for moving the signature across the line. Per our agreement I attached an initial Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the post-signature implementation roadmap: rollout, canary, migration, and training windows. The attachment is a working draft — we expect to iterate after your feedback.

Key proposed milestones (high level):
- Kickoff call (internal + Aperture leads): 2026-05-18
- Technical discovery & provisioning complete: 2026-05-27
- Canary execution (production slice): 2026-06-01 -> 2026-06-07
  - Success criteria: 95% p95 latency under target, zero critical errors, sample QA pass on 500 prompts
- Bulk migration window (data sync + reroute): 2026-06-15
- Enablement & training (train-the-trainer + QA): week of 2026-06-22
- Customer acceptance & closeout: 2026-07-02

Open asks for Aperture:
1) Confirm the internal stakeholders (SRE, Security contact, Training lead) you want on the kickoff invite.
2) Provide the procurement contact for final billing details (we cc'ed contracts@aperturehealth.com as a placeholder).
3) Any constraints on the canary slice size or blackout dates in June?

Attachments: Aperture-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with milestone rows, owners, acceptance criteria)

I'll coordinate the kickoff invite once we have stakeholder names and confirm the Thursday cadence you mentioned.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-signature MAP: phased migration, canary & eval checkpoints (Aperture Health)

Thanks Naomi — this looks like a good starting point. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Canary criteria: can you add a short subsection that spells out the exact traffic percentage and user cohorts we'll route to Redwood for the initial 7-day run? We typically start with 2-3% of traffic and expand, but want the gating conditions written.
- Legal/procurement: I've looped in contracts@aperturehealth.com — they'll review the billing cadence and DocuSign link.
- Weekly sync: Thursday mornings (10:00am PT) works best for our tech and product team; can we lock a recurring 30-min slot starting 2026-05-20?

Also: we have a scheduled maintenance blackout 2026-06-11 -> 2026-06-13 on our primary region — prefer that the bulk migration not overlap with those dates.

Liam / team —

Appreciate the quick reply and the blackout heads-up. I've updated the MAP to add a Canary section with explicit gating criteria and a traffic ramp plan (attached Aperture-MAP-v1.1.xlsx). Summary of the canary gating we propose:
- Start: 2% of production traffic routed to Redwood inference path (cohort: internal beta users + 10% of low-risk external users)
- Day 1 checks: p95 latency < target threshold, error rate < 0.5%, automated QA sample pass >= 90%
- Ramp: 2% -> 5% after 24h if checks pass, 5% -> 10% after next 24h if checks pass
- Rollback: automated traffic cutover to incumbent if any critical error or manual rollback requested by Aperture SRE

Attachments included: Aperture-MAP-v1.1.xlsx (updated milestones + owners), canary-checklist.md (detailed runbook).

I've booked the recurring Thursdays at 10:00am PT starting 2026-05-20 and sent calendar invites to the emails on thread. Naomi — I'll queue the trainer pre-reads and confirm the half-day blocks for the week of 2026-06-22 once Marissa confirms exact trainer availability.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

—Ben
